news.casting_brief: NASA astrophysics director, startup founder/engineers at a space servicing company, mission scientists; high-stakes race-against-time dynamic between bureaucracy and scrappy innovators.
news.script_brief: NASA gives three companies under a year to save a $500M astronomy satellite from crashing. A 2020 startup wins a $30M bet to chase, latch, and reboost the doomed spacecraft. Tension: impossible deadline, tight budget, robotic-arm capture never done before. Beats: the pitch, the contract, the launch, will it work?
news.news_close_brief: With a satellite built in record time now racing to rescue a half-billion-dollar mission, the gamble's outcome remains uncertain. Whether the robotic arms can catch and reboost it is the question that lingers.

dramatic_state.dramatic_question: Can Katalyst's Link spacecraft chase, latch, and reboost the doomed Swift on NASA's impossible deadline before the $500M satellite burns up?
dramatic_state.character_a_wants: Launch Link to latch Swift within NASA's under-a-year deadline, no slip.
dramatic_state.character_b_wants: Delay the launch until the three robotic arms can capture Swift without wrecking it.
dramatic_state.ending_change: Link launches from Wallops Island and its three arms capture Swift, proving startup servicing works just before reentry.
